public_rationale: No decisive qualifying financing event was verified by October 28, 2026. Broad infrastructure-financing targets do not establish annual funding supplied to OpenAI. The forecast has no fixed deadline, so the absence of such an event cannot count as support.
limitations: Private transactions may not be fully disclosed.
Direct financing, supplier financing, and infrastructure lending must be distinguished.
The annual-window and repeatability interpretations could affect an eventual assessment.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Private credit funds cannot stomach supplying OpenAI over $100 billion a year, given its very negative margins and a competitor taking its business.

statement.excerpt: That being said, we’re talking about over $100 billion a year for the foreseeable future, which is a little more than they could stomach on a private company with ultra-negative margins and a younger competitor currently eating its lunch.

from_speaker: a private company with ultra-negative margins
a younger competitor currently eating its lunch
our_interpretation: They refers collectively to private credit funds discussed in the preceding paragraph.
The plain reading is that these funds will not supply OpenAI more than $100 billion in financing within a year at the contemplated scale.
I treat a year as a continuous twelve-month period beginning on or after the post. No calendar or fiscal year was specified.

Count financing actually supplied to OpenAI. Infrastructure financing to another borrower, equity from a different strategy of the same asset manager, and unexecuted fundraising targets do not automatically qualify.
The comments about margins and competition are offered as reasons, not explicit antecedents that must occur before the forecast can be assessed.
Foreseeable future supplies no fixed deadline.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence covering a defined forecast period would need to establish that private credit funds could not or would not supply the stated annual amount. Without an endpoint, temporary non-occurrence cannot conclusively support the forecast.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Verified private credit financing supplied to OpenAI exceeds $100 billion within a qualifying twelve-month period.

evidence.explanation: NVIDIA describes financing decisions made separately for individual opportunities. Its broader capital-mobilization ambition does not establish financing supplied to OpenAI or satisfy the annual threshold.
